learning_outcomes.text: Unified introduction to the scientific fundamentals of Electrical Engineering and essential practical applications: systematic study of electrical or electronic circuits; knowledge of the operation of electrical machines and electrical equipment used in machine construction, their electrical and electronic drive, their use in safe, correct and economical operating conditions; electrical measurement of electrical and magnetic quantities.
Knowledge of the operation of devices built from semiconductor materials and their simple applications.
Ability to select diagrams and components for given applications.
Ability to measure electrical quantities in simple electronic circuits.
Ability to perform calculations, demonstrations and applications for analog electronic devices such as diodes, transistors, operational amplifiers and logic gates.
Acquisition of fundamental knowledge in the field of electrotechnical materials, electrical circuits, and electromagnetic field.
Acquisition of Electrotechnical competences necessary for understanding subsequently taught disciplines.
Broadening of the technical horizon, with the aim of acquiring useful competences for collaborating with other specialists to solve multidisciplinary projects.
Illustration of the engineering approach to concrete problems and development of practical skills, the ability to measure and interpret experimental results.
Electrical equipment used in machine construction is presented, as well as the method of electrical and electronic measurement of circuits used in various equipment.

syllabus_topics: Introductory concepts: Introduction to the main physical quantities and their units of measurement used in electrical engineering; Concepts of electric field; Concepts of magnetic field; Concepts of time-varying electromagnetic field.

Ideal passive elements used in the study of electrical circuits: Ideal resistor; Series/parallel/mixed connection of resistors; Ideal capacitor; Series/parallel/mixed connection of ideal capacitors; Ideal inductor; Magnetically coupled inductors.
Linear and filamentary direct current circuits: Kirchhoff's theorems and their application for calculating circuit currents; Power conservation theorems.

Linear and filamentary sinusoidal steady-state circuits: Behavior of passive elements under sinusoidal excitation; Series RLC circuit; Kirchhoff's theorems for sinusoidal steady state; Powers in sinusoidal steady state; Power factor; Three-phase circuits.
Basic principles of electrical machines: electric transformer, asynchronous motor, direct current machines, operating and usage principles, characteristics, starting and speed control.
Passive components. Resistor, capacitor, inductor, resistive voltage divider.
Diode and diode circuits. Diode structure, forward and reverse bias, symbol, static characteristic, half-wave rectifiers, full-wave rectifiers.
Bipolar transistor. Structure, operation, biasing circuits, small-signal model, bipolar transistor amplifier, frequency band in amplifiers.
Field-effect transistors. Structure, operation, biasing circuits.
Operational amplifier. Symbol, characteristics, ideal operational amplifier, circuits implemented with operational amplifiers, stabilized voltage sources with error amplifier.
Logic circuits. Logic gates and combinational circuits.
Measurement of electrical quantities.
Direct current circuits.
Sinusoidal steady-state circuits.
Single-phase electric transformer.
Squirrel-cage asynchronous motor.
Electronic devices.
Electronic components.
Diode circuits.
Rectifiers.
Integrated circuits.
teaching_methods: Processing and interpretation of experimental results

assessment_methods.method: Practical activities (theoretical knowledge, assembly, measurements, data processing, short tests, presentation of operation and data, work presentation, Q&A)

assessment_rules: Knowledge of fundamental Electrotechnics concepts (quantities, laws, theorems) is required. Students must be able to solve simple direct current and sinusoidal steady-state problems. Correct assembly of a medium complexity circuit according to a given diagram is necessary. Proficiency in reading measuring instruments and correctly interpreting experimental data is also essential.
